note: Seasonal challenges. Same shape as challenges.json - READ, REFLECT, PRAY, and a block for the house - plus a season: a fixed window (startMonth/startDay to endMonth/endDay) or a moveable feast keyed to Easter (lent, holy-week, pentecost). Scripture is a reference only, resolved from the bundled KJV.

challenges.title: 21 Days of Prayer and Fasting
challenges.promise: Give God the first three weeks of the year, and the rest of it with them.

written.title: Sanctify yourselves
written.reflection:
Before Israel crossed the Jordan into a new land, Joshua told them, Sanctify yourselves: for to morrow the LORD will do wonders among you. They prepared first, and then they crossed.

That is what these twenty-one days are for. Many churches begin the year this way, giving God the first weeks before the rush of work and school takes over. You are not trying to earn a good year. You are making room to hear from the God who already holds it.
written.prayer: Father, I give You the start of this year. Before I make my plans, I want to hear Yours. Set me apart for You in these twenty-one days. Clean my heart, quiet my mind, and do wonders among us, as You did for Israel. Prepare me for what You are about to do. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What do you most want from God in these three weeks?
written.familyQuestion: What is one thing we want to ask God for as a family this year?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, we give You this year as a household. Prepare us, and do wonders among us.

written.title: Why we fast
written.reflection:
Ezra was about to lead families on a long, dangerous road. He proclaimed a fast to seek of him a right way for us, and for our little ones. Then he says simply, he was intreated of us.

Fasting is not a hunger strike to force God's hand. It is a way of humbling ourselves and saying, we need You more than we need food. Write down why you are fasting. A clear reason will keep you going on the days your stomach complains.
written.prayer: Lord, I humble myself before You at the start of this year. I need a right way for myself, for my family and for all that I have. I am not fasting to impress You or to bargain with You. I am fasting because I need You. Hear me, as You heard Ezra. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Why are you fasting, in one sentence?
written.familyQuestion: What road is our family about to walk this year?
written.familyPrayer: Father, show us a right way for us and for our little ones, and keep us on it.

written.title: Fast wisely
written.reflection:
Daniel asked to eat only pulse, which is vegetables and grains, and to drink water for ten days. This is where the Daniel fast comes from. Others fast from morning until noon or until evening, or skip one meal a day.

Choose what is wise for your body. Drink water. If you are pregnant, nursing, diabetic, on medication, recovering from illness or have ever struggled with eating, speak to a doctor first, and fast from something other than food instead. Children should not do a food fast. God looks at the heart, not at how hungry you are.
written.prayer: Father, help me to fast with wisdom and not with pride. Show me the fast that is right for my body and my life. Where I am weak, be my strength. Let what I give up make room for You, and let me not harm the body You gave me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What kind of fast is wise for you this year?
written.familyQuestion: How can each of us take part in a way that is right for our age and health?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help each one in this house to seek You in a way that is wise and safe.

written.title: A new thing
written.reflection:
Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old. God told Israel not to stay stuck in what had gone before, good or bad. Behold, I will do a new thing.

Last year may have had losses you are still carrying, or successes you are trying to repeat. Both can keep you looking back. Today, hand last year to God. Thank Him for what was good, grieve what was hard, and then turn and face the way He is making in the wilderness.
written.prayer: Lord, I hand last year to You, all of it. Thank You for every good thing. I bring You what hurt, and I ask You to heal it. Now I turn to face what You are doing. Make a way in my wilderness and rivers in my desert. Do a new thing, and help me to see it. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What from last year do you need to leave behind?
written.familyQuestion: What was the best thing God did for our family last year?
written.familyPrayer: Father, thank You for last year. We trust You with the new thing You are doing.

written.title: Consider your ways
written.reflection:
The people in Haggai's time were busy with their own houses while God's house lay in ruins. They worked hard but never had enough. Twice God says, Consider your ways.

A fast is a good time to look honestly at how you spend your days, your money and your attention. Where has God been put last? This is not about guilt. It is about putting first things first, so that your work is not like wages put into a bag with holes.
written.prayer: Father, I stop and consider my ways. Show me where I have put You last and kept my own house first. I do not want to work hard and still come up empty. Help me to put You first in my time, my money and my heart this year. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where have you been putting God last?
written.familyQuestion: What takes up most of our time as a family?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to put You first in this house, and bless the work of our hands.

written.title: Write the vision
written.reflection:
God told Habakkuk, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables. Some things God shows us need to be written down so we remember them when life gets busy.

Take time today to write what you sense God is saying about this year: for your walk with Him, your family, your work, your church. Keep it short and plain. Then hold it loosely and pray over it. though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come.
written.prayer: Lord, I want to see what You see for this year. Speak to me, and help me to write it down plainly. Where my plans are my own, correct them. Where they are Yours, give me patience to wait and faith to keep going. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What do you sense God saying about this year?
written.familyQuestion: What would we like to see God do in our family this year?
written.familyPrayer: Father, give our house a clear vision, and the patience to wait for it.

written.title: Search me
written.reflection:
Search me, O God, and know my heart. This is a brave prayer. It asks God to look into the places we would rather not look.

Fasting often brings things to the surface: irritation, old resentments, habits we lean on. That is part of its gift. When something comes up today, do not push it away. Bring it to God. He is not searching you to shame you, but to lead me in the way everlasting.
written.prayer: Search me, O God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. Show me any wicked way in me that I have stopped noticing. I confess it to You. Forgive me, cleanse me, and lead me in the way everlasting. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What has come to the surface in you since you started fasting?
written.familyQuestion: Is there anything we need to say sorry to each other for?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, search our home. Where we have hurt each other, help us to make it right.

written.title: Your household
written.reflection:
This psalm pictures a home blessed by God: Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house: thy children like olive plants round about thy table. It begins with every one that feareth the LORD.

Today, pray for your household by name. If you are married, pray for your spouse. If you have children, pray for each one. If you live alone, pray for the family you came from and the people God has placed around you. A blessed home starts with someone who prays for it.
written.prayer: Father, I bring my household to You. I pray for each one by name. Bless our home with peace. Let it be a place where You are honoured, where love is patient and words are kind. Keep us from anything that would divide us. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who in your household needs prayer most right now?
written.familyQuestion: What is one thing each of us is thankful for about our home?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, bless this house. Let peace live here, and let You be honoured at our table.

written.title: Your children
written.reflection:
all thy children shall be taught of the LORD; and great shall be the peace of thy children. Many parents pray this verse over their children every year.

Pray today for your children, or for the children in your family and church. Pray that they would know God for themselves, not only through you. Pray for their schooling, their friends and their future. If you have no children, pray for a young person you know. They need people praying for them.
written.prayer: Lord, I bring the children in my life to You. Teach them Yourself. Let them know You, not just know about You. Give them peace, protect them from harm, and guide them in their studies and friendships. Let them grow up to love You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Which young person will you pray for by name today?
written.familyQuestion: What do our children want God to help them with this year?
written.familyPrayer: Father, teach our children Yourself, and give them great peace.

written.title: Health
written.reflection:
John wrote to his friend Gaius, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth. He cared about the whole person, body and soul.

Pray today for your health and the health of those you love. Pray for anyone who is sick. Health is a gift from God, and caring for it is part of being faithful. If fasting is making you unwell, stop and eat. God would rather have you healthy and praying than unwell and proud.
written.prayer: Father, thank You for the body You have given me. I pray for health this year, for myself and for my family. I bring You everyone I know who is sick. Heal them, comfort them and give wisdom to those who care for them. Help me to look after my body well. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who do you know who needs prayer for healing?
written.familyQuestion: What could we do this year to look after our health as a family?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, keep this family in good health, and heal those we love who are sick.

written.title: Work and provision
written.reflection:
The LORD shall command the blessing upon thee in thy storehouses, and in all that thou settest thine hand unto. God cares about our work and our provision. He wants His people to have enough, and to be able to help others.

Pray today about your work, your business or your search for work. Pray about debts and bills. Ask God for honest gain and wisdom with money. And pray for people you know who are without work this year.
written.prayer: Lord, I bring my work and my finances to You. Bless the work of my hands. Give me favour, wisdom and honest gain. Help me to clear my debts and to be generous. Provide for those I know who are struggling to find work. You are my provider. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What do you need God to do in your work or finances this year?
written.familyQuestion: How could our family be more generous this year?
written.familyPrayer: Father, bless the work of our hands, and make us a family that gives.

written.title: Power to the faint
written.reflection:
You are more than halfway, and this is often where it gets hard. The excitement of day one has worn off. He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.

If you have slipped a day or two, do not give up. Simply begin again today. God is not counting your failures. The ones who wait upon the Lord are not the ones who never get tired. They are the ones who keep coming back to Him when they do.
written.prayer: Lord, I am tired. I have not done this perfectly. But I come back to You today. Give power to me where I am faint, and increase my strength where I have none. Help me to finish these days well, not by my might but by Yours. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What has been hardest about these first eleven days?
written.familyQuestion: How can we encourage each other to keep going?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, when we are tired, give us Your strength. Help us to finish well together.

written.title: Your going out and coming in
written.reflection:
The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore. People pray this over their travel, their roads, their homes.

Pray today for protection for yourself and your family: on the roads, at work, at school and at home. Pray for those who travel often. Fear does not have to rule this year. The Lord is thy keeper, and He does not sleep.
written.prayer: Father, I ask You to keep me and my family this year. Preserve our going out and our coming in. Protect us on the roads and in our homes. Keep us from all evil. Where we are afraid, remind us that You are our keeper and You never sleep. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where do you most need God's protection this year?
written.familyQuestion: Who in our family travels often, and how can we pray for them?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, keep our going out and our coming in, and bring each of us home safely.

written.title: The church
written.reflection:
The early believers continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers. They shared meals, cared for each other and praised God, and the Lord added to their number daily.

Pray today for your church: your pastors and leaders, the people in your congregation, and those who have drifted away. Pray that this year your church would be a family where people are fed, loved and sent out.
written.prayer: Lord, I pray for my church. Bless our pastors and leaders with wisdom and strength. Make us a family that prays, learns and cares for one another. Bring back those who have drifted. Add to us daily such as should be saved. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who in your church could you encourage this week?
written.familyQuestion: What do we love about our church?
written.familyPrayer: Father, bless our church family, and help us to play our part in it.

written.title: Heal our land
written.reflection:
If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

The healing of a nation begins with God's own people humbling themselves. Pray today for your country, whichever it is. Pray about its troubles, its poverty, its violence and its divisions. Then ask God what part He wants you to play.
written.prayer: Lord, I humble myself and pray for my nation. Forgive us where we have turned from You. Heal our land. Bring peace where there is violence, provision where there is hunger, and honesty where there is corruption. Begin with Your people, and begin with me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What does your nation most need from God this year?
written.familyQuestion: What can our family do to be a blessing in our community?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, heal our land, and make our home a light in our community.

written.title: Those in authority
written.reflection:
Paul asks that prayers be made For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life. He wrote this when the rulers were not believers and were often unjust.

Praying for leaders is not the same as agreeing with them. Pray today for your president or prime minister, your local leaders, judges, police and those who run schools and hospitals. Pray that they would act with wisdom and justice, and that God would turn hearts toward what is right.
written.prayer: Father, I pray for all who are in authority over my nation and my community. Give them wisdom, honesty and a heart for justice. Where they are doing wrong, turn their hearts. Where they are doing right, strengthen them. Let us live quiet and peaceable lives. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Which leader do you find hardest to pray for?
written.familyQuestion: Who are the leaders in our community we could pray for together?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, give wisdom to those who lead us, and peace to our land.

written.title: No weapon
written.reflection:
No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper. This is a favourite verse in many churches, and rightly so. But notice how it ends: This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is of me.

Our protection is not a magic word. It rests on belonging to God and on the righteousness He gives. Whatever has been spoken against you, whatever you fear, bring it to Him. He is the one who establishes you.
written.prayer: Lord, I bring to You every fear, every evil word spoken against me and every plan against my life. I stand in the righteousness You have given me in Christ. Let no weapon formed against me prosper. Establish me in Your peace, far from terror. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What are you afraid might come against you this year?
written.familyQuestion: What does it mean that we belong to God?
written.familyPrayer: Father, we belong to You. Protect this house, and keep us from fear.

written.title: He goes before you
written.reflection:
God spoke to Cyrus, a king who did not yet know Him: I will go before thee, and make the crooked places straight: I will break in pieces the gates of brass. If God would go before a king who did not know Him, how much more will He go before His own children?

Is there a door that has been shut for a long time? A situation that seems locked? Bring it to God today. He is able to go ahead of you and make a way.
written.prayer: Father, go before me this year. Make the crooked places straight. Where doors have been shut, open them if it is Your will. Where gates have held me back, break them. And where You close a door, give me peace to trust You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What closed door do you want to bring to God?
written.familyQuestion: Where do we need God to go before us as a family?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, go ahead of us this year, and make a way where there seems to be none.

written.title: Not by might
written.reflection:
Zerubbabel faced a great mountain of a task: rebuilding the temple with few people and little money. God's word to him was, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.

After nearly three weeks of prayer and fasting, it is tempting to think the results depend on how hard you have tried. They do not. The work is done by God's Spirit. Pray today to be filled with the Holy Spirit, and to rely on Him all year.
written.prayer: Holy Spirit, fill me afresh. I cannot do what this year will ask of me by my own strength. Let everything I do be done by Your Spirit. Make my mountains plains, and let me give the glory to God alone. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What mountain in your life needs the Spirit's help, not more effort?
written.familyQuestion: Where do we try to do things in our own strength as a family?
written.familyPrayer: Holy Spirit, fill this house, and help us to rely on You.

written.title: Crown the year
written.reflection:
Thou crownest the year with thy goodness. The psalmist pictures fields watered, valleys full of corn, hills rejoicing. It is a picture of a year God has blessed.

Today, give thanks in advance. Thank God for what He has already done in these twenty days, for answers you have seen and for those still on the way. Gratitude before the answer is a mark of faith. It says, I trust You to finish what You have started.
written.prayer: Father, thank You. Thank You for these days with You, for what You have shown me and for prayers You have already answered. I thank You in advance for what You will do this year. Crown this year with Your goodness. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What has God already done during these twenty days?
written.familyQuestion: What are we thanking God for in advance this year?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You for this year. Crown it with Your goodness.

written.title: From the beginning of the year
written.reflection:
Moses described the land God was giving His people as A land which the LORD thy God careth for: the eyes of the LORD thy God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year even unto the end of the year.

The fast ends today. Break it gently, with light food. But do not leave the closeness behind. Choose one habit from these three weeks to keep: a morning prayer, a weekly fast, a Bible reading. God's eyes will be on you all year, not just in January.
written.prayer: Father, thank You for these twenty-one days. As I end this fast, I do not want to end this nearness. Keep Your eyes on me from the beginning of the year to the end. Help me to keep the habits that have drawn me close to You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What one habit from these three weeks will you keep?
written.familyQuestion: How will we keep praying together after today?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, Your eyes are on us all year. Keep us close to You until the very end of it.

challenges.title: Forty Days to Easter
challenges.promise: Forty days to slow down, turn back to God, and walk with Jesus to the cross and the empty tomb.

written.title: Dust
written.reflection:
for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return. Many Christians begin these forty days by remembering that we are made of dust. It sounds grim, but it is honest. Life is short and we are not God.

That honesty is where this season starts. Not with trying harder, but with admitting our need. The God who formed us from the dust is the same God who came in Jesus to raise us from it. Lent ends at an empty tomb.
written.prayer: Lord, I remember today that I am dust. My life is short and my strength is small. I need You. Over these forty days, turn me back to You. Teach me to number my days, and walk with me all the way to the cross and the empty tomb. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What would you change if you remembered how short life is?
written.familyQuestion: What does it mean that God made us from dust?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You for making us. Walk with our family these forty days.

written.title: While He may be found
written.reflection:
Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near. God is near today. He is not hard to find for those who turn to Him.

The invitation is open to the wicked and the unrighteous. let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon. Abundantly. Whatever you bring into these forty days, His pardon is bigger. Decide today what you will set aside to make room for Him.
written.prayer: Father, I seek You today while You are near. I turn from my own ways and my own thoughts, and I return to You. Thank You that You abundantly pardon. Show me what to set aside in this season so that I can make more room for You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What will you set aside this Lent to make room for God?
written.familyQuestion: Is there something we could give up or take up together as a family?
written.familyPrayer: Father, we seek You together. Thank You that You are near.

written.title: Wash me
written.reflection:
David wrote this after his sin with Bathsheba was exposed. He does not make excuses. Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. He appeals not to his own goodness but to God's lovingkindness and the multitude of thy tender mercies.

Repentance is not wallowing. It is telling God the truth and trusting His mercy. Lent gives us time to do this slowly and honestly, without hurrying past what is wrong.
written.prayer: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to Your lovingkindness. I acknowledge my sin; I will not hide it from You. Wash me thoroughly and cleanse me. I trust not in my goodness but in the multitude of Your tender mercies. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What do you need to be honest with God about?
written.familyQuestion: How do we say sorry well in this house?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, wash our hearts. Help us to be honest with You and with each other.

written.title: Led into the wilderness
written.reflection:
Lent is forty days because Jesus spent forty days in the wilderness. He was full of the Holy Ghost and led by the Spirit, and He was hungry. When the devil tempted Him to turn stone into bread, He answered, man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

If you are fasting from something this Lent, you will feel the lack. Let that feeling turn you to God's word. Read a little more. Listen a little longer.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You went into the wilderness for me. When I feel hungry for what I have given up, turn me to Your word. Teach me that I do not live by bread alone. Feed me with every word that comes from God. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What are you hungry for that only God can satisfy?
written.familyQuestion: What Bible story could we read together this week?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, feed this family with Your word as well as our daily bread.

written.title: Him only
written.reflection:
The devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and offered them, if only Jesus would worship him. It was a shortcut to power without the cross.

Jesus refused: Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. We are offered shortcuts too: success without integrity, comfort without obedience. Every shortcut asks us to bow to something other than God. This week, notice what you are tempted to bow to.
written.prayer: Lord, I worship You, and You only will I serve. Show me the shortcuts I am tempted to take, the places where I am bowing to something other than You. Give me the strength Jesus had to say no. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What shortcut are you tempted to take?
written.familyQuestion: What things compete for first place in our home?
written.familyPrayer: Father, You alone are God in this house. Help us to serve You first.

written.title: For a season
written.reflection:
The devil even quoted Scripture to Jesus, twisting a promise into a dare. Jesus answered with Scripture rightly understood: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.

Then the devil departed from him for a season. Temptation comes back. Jesus did not win once and never face it again, and neither will we. But each time we resist, we learn that God's word is strong enough. Knowing it well helps us notice when it is being bent.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You faced every temptation and did not fall. When temptation returns to me, remind me of Your word. Keep me from twisting Scripture to suit myself. Make me ready for the next season of testing. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Which temptation keeps coming back to you?
written.familyQuestion: What verse could we learn together this week?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, hide Your word in our hearts so that we do not sin against You.

written.title: To know what was in thine heart
written.reflection:
Moses told Israel to remember the forty years in the wilderness. God led them there to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart.

Hard seasons show us what is in us. They also show us God's care. Israel was hungry, and God fed them with manna, something they had never known. If you are in a wilderness now, God has not abandoned you. He is teaching you and feeding you in ways you may only see later.
written.prayer: Father, I remember all the ways You have led me, including the hard ones. Humble me, and show me what is in my heart. Feed me in this wilderness. Teach me that I live by every word that comes out of Your mouth. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What has a hard season shown you about your own heart?
written.familyQuestion: When has God taken care of our family in a hard time?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You for leading us and feeding us, even in the wilderness.

written.title: He understands
written.reflection:
we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.

Jesus knows what temptation feels like. He knows hunger, tiredness, loneliness and pressure. So when you fail, you do not come to a judge who cannot understand. You come to a friend who was tempted in every way and stayed faithful. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You understand my weakness. You were tempted as I am, yet You did not sin. I come boldly to Your throne of grace today. I need mercy for where I have failed and grace to help me now. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where do you need grace to help in time of need?
written.familyQuestion: How does it help to know Jesus understands how we feel?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, thank You that You understand us. Help us when we are weak.

written.title: Blessed is the man that endureth
written.reflection:
Blessed is the man that endureth temptation. James is honest about where temptation comes from. It is not from God. It grows from our own desires. every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

Sin starts small, as a desire we entertain, and grows. That is why it is wise to deal with it early, while it is still a thought. What desire have you been entertaining that you know will lead somewhere you do not want to go?
written.prayer: Father, I confess that temptation often grows from my own desires. Show me the small thoughts that lead to sin, and help me to deal with them early. Give me strength to endure, and keep me for the crown of life You have promised. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What small desire do you need to deal with early?
written.familyQuestion: What helps us say no to things we know are wrong?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, give us strength to say no to wrong and yes to You.

written.title: Remember not
written.reflection:
Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions: according to thy mercy remember thou me. David asks God to forget some things and remember others. Forget my sins. Remember me, according to Your mercy.

Some of us carry regrets from years ago. We remember them clearly, and we assume God does too. But when we confess, God chooses to remember us by His mercy, not by our failures. You can pray this prayer for yourself today.
written.prayer: Lord, remember not the sins of my youth. I bring You the regrets I still carry. According to Your mercy, remember me. Show me Your ways, teach me Your paths, and lead me in Your truth. On You I wait all the day. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What old regret do you need to hand to God?
written.familyQuestion: How does God want us to treat each other's past mistakes?
written.familyPrayer: Father, remember us by Your mercy. Help us to forgive each other too.

written.title: Take up his cross daily
written.reflection:
If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. Daily. Following Jesus is not one big decision made once. It is a choice we make every morning.

Denying yourself does not mean hating yourself. It means saying no to the self that wants its own way above everything, so that you can say yes to Jesus. what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, I choose to follow You today. Help me to deny myself where my own way pulls me from You. I take up my cross for today. Keep me from gaining the world and losing my soul. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What does taking up your cross look like today?
written.familyQuestion: What is one way we can put others first this week?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, help each of us to follow You today, one day at a time.

written.title: He set His face
written.reflection:
he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem. Jesus knew what waited for Him there. He went anyway, because He came to save.

On the way, a village refused Him, and James and John wanted to call down fire. Jesus rebuked them. the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. Even on His way to the cross, He was teaching His followers mercy. Set your face toward Him, and keep walking.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You set Your face toward Jerusalem for me. Help me to set my face toward You and not turn back. When I want to call down fire on those who reject me, teach me Your mercy. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where are you tempted to turn back from following Jesus?
written.familyQuestion: How should we treat people who are unkind to us?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, give us mercy for people who do not treat us well.

written.title: Count the cost
written.reflection:
Jesus did not want followers who start well and quit when it gets hard. He told of a man who began to build a tower without counting the cost, and could not finish.

Following Jesus costs something. It may cost comfort, reputation, relationships or plans. Jesus is honest about that. He would rather we count the cost and follow with our eyes open than be surprised later. And He promises that what we gain in Him is worth far more.
written.prayer: Lord, I count the cost of following You, and I still choose You. Where it costs me comfort or approval, give me courage. Help me to finish what I have begun with You, and not to give up halfway. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What has following Jesus cost you?
written.familyQuestion: What does it cost our family to follow Jesus?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to follow You all the way, not only when it is easy.

written.title: Loss for Christ
written.reflection:
Paul had a great deal to be proud of. He gave it all up and said, I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord.

It is easy to think of Lent as giving things up. Paul shows us why: not because those things are worthless in themselves, but because knowing Christ is worth more. That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection. What you give up is small next to who you gain.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, I want to know You more than anything. Show me what I am holding on to that keeps me from You. Help me to count it loss for the excellency of knowing You. Let me know the power of Your resurrection. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What are you most proud of, and how does it compare with knowing Christ?
written.familyQuestion: What do we love about Jesus?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, we want to know You more. Help us to love You above everything.

written.title: One thing thou lackest
written.reflection:
A young man ran to Jesus asking how to inherit eternal life. He had kept the commandments since his youth. Then Jesus beholding him loved him. Notice that. Jesus loved him before He challenged him.

Then Jesus put His finger on the one thing that held him: his wealth. The man went away grieved. Jesus does not ask everyone to sell everything. But He does ask each of us about the one thing we cannot let go. He asks because He loves us.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You look at me and love me. Show me the one thing I lack, the one thing I hold on to more tightly than You. Give me grace not to walk away grieved but to follow You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What is the one thing you find hardest to give to Jesus?
written.familyQuestion: What do we find hard to share?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, thank You that You love us. Help us to hold our things loosely.

written.title: Whom say ye?
written.reflection:
People had many opinions about Jesus. Some said a prophet. Some said John the Baptist come back. Jesus asked His disciples, But whom say ye that I am?

Peter answered, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God. Halfway through Lent, this is the question that matters most. Not what your parents believe, or your church, or the people around you, but what you say. Who is Jesus to you?
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. I confess You today, not because others do but because I believe it. Help my faith to be my own. Show me more of who You are. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who do you say Jesus is?
written.familyQuestion: If someone asked each of us who Jesus is, what would we say?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, You are the Son of God. Help each one in this house to know You for themselves.

written.title: The one that was lost
written.reflection:
The religious leaders complained that Jesus welcomed sinners and ate with them. So He told them about a shepherd who left ninety-nine sheep to look for one that was lost, and carried it home on his shoulders rejoicing.

joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth. God is not reluctant to take you back. He comes looking. And when He finds you, He does not drive you home. He carries you, rejoicing.
written.prayer: Father, thank You that You came looking for me. When I wander, find me again. Thank You that heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents. I come home to You today. Carry me on Your shoulders. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Have you ever felt like the one lost sheep?
written.familyQuestion: Who do we know who might feel lost and far from God?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, find those we love who have wandered, and bring them home rejoicing.

written.title: Seek diligently
written.reflection:
A woman lost one silver coin. She lit a candle, swept the house and searched carefully until she found it. Then she called her neighbours to celebrate.

The coin did nothing to be found. It just lay there in the dust. That is grace. God searches for us when we cannot search for Him. If you have someone you love who is far from God, take heart. He is searching for them with more care than you are. Keep praying.
written.prayer: Lord, thank You that You searched for me when I could not find my way to You. I pray for those I love who are far from You. Light a candle, sweep the house, and search for them until they are found. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who are you praying will be found by God?
written.familyQuestion: What do we feel like when we find something we lost?
written.familyPrayer: Father, search for the people we love, and bring them back to You.

written.title: God be merciful to me
written.reflection:
Two men prayed in the temple. One listed his good works and thanked God he was not like other people. The other stood at a distance, would not even look up, and smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner.

Jesus said the second man went home justified. The prayer God hears is not the impressive one. It is the honest one. You can pray the tax collector's prayer today, and mean it.
written.prayer: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. I do not come with a list of good works. I come with my need. Forgive me for every time I have looked down on others. Thank You that You hear the honest prayer. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who do you secretly feel better than?
written.familyQuestion: Why does God like honest prayers?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, make us humble. Help us not to look down on anyone.

written.title: Godly sorrow
written.reflection:
Paul had written a hard letter, and the church was grieved by it. But he rejoiced, because their sorrow led to change. godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

There is a sorrow that only beats us down: shame, self-hatred, regret that goes nowhere. And there is a sorrow that turns us back to God and leads to life. If you feel sorry for your sin, let it lead you to Him, not away.
written.prayer: Father, I am sorry for my sin. Let this sorrow lead me to You and not to despair. Take away the shame that only beats me down. Give me the godly sorrow that leads to repentance and life. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Does your sorrow over sin lead you to God or away from Him?
written.familyQuestion: What should we do when we feel bad about something we did?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, when we do wrong, help us to come to You and not hide.

written.title: Depths of the sea
written.reflection:
Micah asks who is a God like this, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression. He is amazed at God's mercy. he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy.

Then he says that God will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea. Not near the shore where they can wash back up, but into the depths. Some people say God puts up a sign there: no fishing. Stop going back for what He has already thrown away.
written.prayer: Lord, who is a God like You? Thank You that You delight in mercy. Thank You that You have cast my sins into the depths of the sea. Help me to stop fishing for what You have forgiven. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What forgiven sin do you keep going back to?
written.familyQuestion: What does it mean that God delights in mercy?
written.familyPrayer: Father, thank You that You love to forgive. Help us to forgive like You.

written.title: East from the west
written.reflection:
He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities. If God gave us what we deserve, none of us could stand.

Instead, As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us. North and south meet at the poles. East and west never meet. You can travel east for ever and never arrive at west. That is how far your forgiven sin has been removed.
written.prayer: Father, thank You that You have not dealt with me according to my sins. Thank You that Your mercy is as high as the heavens. Thank You that You have removed my sin as far as the east is from the west. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: How does it feel to know your sin has been removed that far?
written.familyQuestion: Can we think of how far east is from west?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You for Your great mercy to our family.

written.title: Faithful and just
written.reflection:
If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves. The first step is honesty. Then comes the promise: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

Faithful, because He keeps His promise. Just, because Jesus has already paid for those sins. Forgiveness is not God bending the rules. It is God keeping His word. Confess today, and believe that you are clean.
written.prayer: Father, I will not pretend that I have no sin. I confess my sins to You now. Thank You that You are faithful and just to forgive me and to cleanse me from all unrighteousness. I believe that I am clean. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What do you need to confess today?
written.familyQuestion: Why is it good to tell the truth about what we have done?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You that You forgive us when we are honest with You.

written.title: Face like a flint
written.reflection:
This is a picture of the servant of the Lord, fulfilled in Jesus. I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting.

He did not shrink back. therefore have I set my face like a flint. Jesus knew the suffering ahead and did not turn away. He also knew how to speak a word in season to him that is weary. He is strong enough to suffer for you and gentle enough to speak to you when you are tired.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You set Your face like a flint and did not hide from shame. Thank You for suffering for me. Thank You also for knowing how to speak a word to me when I am weary. Speak to me today. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where do you need a word from God for your weariness?
written.familyQuestion: How was Jesus brave for us?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, thank You for being brave for us. Make us brave too.

written.title: He humbled Himself
written.reflection:
Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus. Paul describes the downward steps of Jesus: from equality with God, to the form of a servant, to the likeness of men, to death, and not just any death, even the death of the cross.

This is the shape of His love. He kept going down so that He could lift us up. And Paul says, let this mind be in you. Humility is not thinking badly of yourself. It is being willing to go low for others.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You humbled Yourself all the way to the cross. Let Your mind be in me. Where I want to be first, teach me to serve. Where I want to be seen, teach me to go low for others. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where could you go low for someone else this week?
written.familyQuestion: How can we serve each other at home this week?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, You served us. Help us to serve one another.

written.title: A ransom for many
written.reflection:
The disciples were arguing about who would be greatest. Jesus said the world's leaders lord it over people, but so shall it not be among you. In His kingdom, the great serve.

Then He explained why: even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many. Jesus was on His way to pay the price to set us free. Every act of service we offer flows from what He gave first.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You came to serve and to give Your life as a ransom for me. Free me from wanting to be greatest. Show me how to serve at home, at work and in church this week. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where are you tempted to want to be the greatest?
written.familyQuestion: Who could we serve together this week?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, make our family a family that serves.

written.title: A corn of wheat
written.reflection:
Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit. Jesus was speaking of His own death. A seed must be buried before it grows. From His death would come life for the world.

The same pattern runs through our lives. Some things must die in us before new life can grow: pride, control, old ways. It is painful, but it is not the end. It is how fruit comes.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You fell into the ground and died so that I could live. Show me what needs to die in me so that new life can grow. I trust You with the burying, because I trust You with the harvest. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What might God be asking to die in you so that something new can grow?
written.familyQuestion: What happens to a seed after we plant it?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to trust You when things are hard, because You bring new life.

written.title: The good shepherd
written.reflection:
I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep. A hired hand runs when the wolf comes. A shepherd stays, because the sheep are his.

Jesus is not a hired hand. You are His. I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine. He knows you by name. And He did not just risk His life for you; He laid it down. No one took it from Him. He gave it.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are my good shepherd. Thank You that You know me and that You laid down Your life for me. When the wolf comes, You do not run. Help me to know Your voice and to follow You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What does it mean to you that Jesus knows you?
written.familyQuestion: What does a good shepherd do for his sheep?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, our good shepherd, keep our family close to You.

written.title: With His stripes
written.reflection:
Written centuries before Jesus, this passage reads like an eyewitness account of the cross. he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities.

All we like sheep have gone astray. All of us. Not some. And the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all. What should have fallen on us fell on Him. That is the heart of the gospel. Read these three verses slowly today, and put your own name in them.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You were wounded for my transgressions and bruised for my iniquities. I have gone astray like a sheep. Thank You that the Father laid my sin on You. By Your stripes I am healed. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What does it mean to you that Jesus took your place?
written.familyQuestion: Why did Jesus have to suffer?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, thank You for taking our place on the cross.

written.title: While we were yet sinners
written.reflection:
Paul says it would be rare for someone to die for a good person. But Christ died for the ungodly. God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

God did not wait for us to improve. He did not love us because we were lovable. He loved us at our worst, and proved it at the cross. You never have to wonder whether God loves you. He has already shown you.
written.prayer: Father, thank You that You loved me while I was still a sinner. I did not earn it. You proved Your love at the cross before I ever turned to You. Help me to rest in that love today. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Do you ever doubt that God loves you?
written.familyQuestion: How did God show that He loves us?
written.familyPrayer: Father, thank You for loving us even when we were far from You.

written.title: In deed and in truth
written.reflection:
Hereby perceive we the love of God, because he laid down his life for us. Then John draws the line straight to us: we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.

He makes it practical. If someone has enough and sees a brother in need and shuts his heart, how can God's love be in him? let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth. What need around you could you meet this week?
written.prayer: Lord, You laid down Your life for me. Help me to lay down my life for others in practical ways. Open my eyes to the needs around me, and open my heart and my hands. Let me love in deed and in truth. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What need around you could you meet this week?
written.familyQuestion: Who could we help as a family this week?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, show us someone to help, and give us generous hearts.

written.title: The least of these
written.reflection:
Jesus described the King welcoming people who had fed the hungry, given drink to the thirsty, welcomed strangers, clothed the naked and visited the sick and the prisoner.

They were surprised. When did we do this for You? Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Jesus hides Himself in the people we might overlook. Look for Him there this week.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me to see You in the people I overlook: the hungry, the stranger, the sick, the prisoner. Give me courage and kindness to serve them. Let what I do for them be done for You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who are the least of these around you?
written.familyQuestion: Who do we see every week who might need kindness?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, help us to see You in the people who need help.

written.title: Search and try our ways
written.reflection:
Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the LORD. Jeremiah wrote this in the ruins of Jerusalem. He did not only blame others. He called his people to look at themselves.

We are nearing the end of these forty days. It is a good moment to look back. What has God shown you? What have you turned from? What still needs turning? Let us lift up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens.
written.prayer: Lord, I search and try my ways before You. Show me what has changed and what still needs to change. I turn again to You. I lift up my heart with my hands to You in the heavens. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What has God shown you during this Lent?
written.familyQuestion: What have we learned about God these past weeks?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You for what You have taught us. Keep turning our hearts to You.

written.title: He will bind us up
written.reflection:
Come, and let us return unto the LORD: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up.

Sometimes God allows things that hurt in order to bring us back. But He does not leave us torn. in the third day he will raise us up. Long before Easter, Hosea spoke of a third day. God's purpose is always healing and new life. he shall come unto us as the rain.
written.prayer: Lord, I return to You. Where I am torn, heal me. Where I am wounded, bind me up. Revive me, raise me up, and let me live in Your sight. Come to me like the rain. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where do you need God to bind you up?
written.familyQuestion: What does rain do for dry ground?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, come to our family like rain, and make us grow.

written.title: My soul longeth
written.reflection:
My soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of the LORD: my heart and my flesh crieth out for the living God.

The psalmist envies the sparrow that builds a nest near God's altar. He just wants to be close. After weeks of setting things aside, some people find that the longing for God has grown. If that is you, give thanks. If you feel nothing, ask Him to give you the longing. He gives it to those who ask.
written.prayer: Lord, I want to want You more. Give me a heart that longs for You and cries out for the living God. Let me be like the sparrow, at home near Your altar. Blessed are they who dwell in Your house. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Has your longing for God grown or faded these past weeks?
written.familyQuestion: Where do we feel close to God?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, give our family hearts that long to be near You.

written.title: The resurrection and the life
written.reflection:
Martha's brother Lazarus had been dead four days. Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live.

Then He asked her, Believest thou this? It is a question for you too. As Lent draws close to the cross, we remember that the cross is not the end. The One who goes to die is the resurrection and the life. Death has no final word over those who believe in Him.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the resurrection and the life. I believe this. Thank You that death does not have the final word over me or over those I love who rest in You. Strengthen my faith as I come close to the cross. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: If Jesus asked you, believest thou this, what would you say?
written.familyQuestion: What did Jesus do for Lazarus?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, You are the resurrection and the life. We believe in You.

written.title: He wept over it
written.reflection:
Jesus rode into Jerusalem to shouts of praise. The crowd cried, Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of the Lord. But when He saw the city, He wept over it.

He knew they did not understand the things which belong unto thy peace. The same crowd would soon turn on Him. Jesus weeps over cities and people who miss Him, even while they praise Him. He sees beneath the noise. Let Him see beneath yours.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, I welcome You as my King. But look beneath my praise and see my heart. Show me the things that belong to my peace. I pray for my city and my nation, that we would know You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Do you know the things that belong to your peace?
written.familyQuestion: Why did Jesus cry over the city?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, our King, we welcome You into our home.

written.title: This do in remembrance
written.reflection:
On the night before He died, Jesus shared the Passover with His disciples. He said, With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you. He wanted to be with them.

Then He took bread and said, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me. Whatever your church calls it, the Lord's Supper, Communion or the Eucharist, it began here, with Jesus longing to be with His friends and giving Himself for them.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You longed to be with Your friends, and that You long to be with me. Thank You for Your body given for me and Your blood shed for me. I remember You today. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What does it mean to you that Jesus wanted to be with His disciples?
written.familyQuestion: What did Jesus do with the bread and the cup?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, thank You for giving Yourself for us. We remember You.

written.title: Into Thy hands
written.reflection:
Darkness covered the land from the sixth hour to the ninth. The veil in the temple was torn in two. Then Jesus cried out, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.

Even in death, He trusted His Father. The torn veil means the way to God is now open. A Roman soldier watching it all said, Certainly this was a righteous man. Stay at the cross a while today. Do not rush to Sunday. Look at what He has done.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, I stand at Your cross. You trusted Your Father even in death. Thank You that the veil is torn and the way to God is open. I commend my spirit into the Father's hands too. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What do you see when you look at the cross?
written.familyQuestion: Why was the veil in the temple torn?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, thank You for dying for us. Thank You that we can come close to God.

written.title: They rested
written.reflection:
Joseph of Arimathaea, a good man who also himself waited for the kingdom of God, took Jesus' body down and laid it in a new tomb. The women watched where He was laid, went home, prepared spices, and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment.

This is the quiet day between the cross and the resurrection. The disciples did not know what was coming. Many of us live in days like this, waiting with no answer yet. Rest today. Sunday is coming.
written.prayer: Lord, today I wait at the tomb with Your friends. I do not always understand the silent days. But I trust that You are at work even when nothing seems to be happening. Thank You that Sunday is coming. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What are you waiting for in silence right now?
written.familyQuestion: How do you think Jesus' friends felt on this day?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to trust You on quiet days. Thank You that Sunday is coming.

challenges.title: Holy Week
challenges.promise: Eight days with Jesus, from the palm branches to the empty tomb.

written.title: Palm Sunday: Who is this?
written.reflection:
Crowds spread their clothes and branches on the road and shouted, Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord. The whole city was stirred, asking, Who is this?

Jesus came riding on a donkey, not a war horse. He came as a King of peace. Many in that crowd wanted a different kind of king, one who would fight their enemies. This week asks the same question of us: who is this Jesus, and what kind of King will we let Him be?
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, Hosanna. Blessed are You who come in the name of the Lord. I welcome You as my King, not the king I would design, but the King You are. Come into my life this week as You came into Jerusalem. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What kind of King do you want Jesus to be?
written.familyQuestion: Why did people wave branches for Jesus?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, we welcome You as our King. Hosanna!

written.title: Monday: A house of prayer
written.reflection:
The day after He entered Jerusalem, Jesus went into the temple and overturned the tables of the moneychangers. My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves.

The court where this trading went on was the only place where foreigners could come to pray. Jesus was angry because people were being shut out from God. Today, ask Him to clear out anything in your heart, or your church, that keeps others from coming to Him.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, come into the temple of my heart and overturn what does not belong there. Make my life a house of prayer. Where I or my church have made it hard for others to find You, forgive us and clear the way. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What needs to be cleared out of your heart this week?
written.familyQuestion: How can we make our home a place of prayer?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, make our home a house of prayer where everyone is welcome.

written.title: Tuesday: The first commandment
written.reflection:
During the last week, the religious leaders tried to trap Jesus with questions. One scribe asked sincerely which commandment was first.

Jesus answered, thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength. Then He added the second: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. In a few days He would show what that love looks like, loving God and loving us all the way to the cross.
written.prayer: Lord, I want to love You with all my heart, soul, mind and strength. Show me where my love for You is divided. Help me to love my neighbour as myself this week, especially the one I find hardest to love. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Which part of you, heart, soul, mind or strength, finds it hardest to love God?
written.familyQuestion: Who is our neighbour?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to love You with everything, and to love our neighbours too.

written.title: Wednesday: She hath done what she could
written.reflection:
In Bethany, a woman broke a jar of costly ointment and poured it on Jesus' head. Some said it was a waste. Jesus said, Let her alone. Then: She hath done what she could.

She gave her best, and Jesus said it would be remembered wherever the gospel was preached. Love for Jesus can look extravagant to others. It does not count the cost. What could you pour out for Him today, not because it is required, but because He is worth it?
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are worth everything. Like this woman, I want to pour out my best for You, even if others call it waste. Show me what I can give You today out of love. Let me do what I can. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What could you give Jesus today out of love?
written.familyQuestion: What is something precious we could give to Jesus?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, You are worth our very best. We give You our love.

written.title: Thursday: Love one another
written.reflection:
On the night He was betrayed, after washing His disciples' feet, Jesus said, A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you.

As I have loved you. That is the measure: a love that kneels and serves, a love that goes to the cross. Then He said, By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples. Not by our arguments or our buildings, but by how we love each other.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for loving me to the end. Help me to love others as You have loved me. Where I have been cold or proud toward other believers, forgive me. Let people know I am Your disciple by my love. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who do you find hardest to love in your church or family?
written.familyQuestion: How can we show love to each other tonight?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, help us to love each other the way You love us.

written.title: Good Friday: Remember me
written.reflection:
Two criminals were crucified with Jesus. One mocked Him. The other said, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.

He had nothing to offer. No good works, no time left to change. Just a request. And Jesus answered, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise. This is the gospel at its simplest. Salvation is not earned. It is asked for, and freely given, by a dying Saviour who still had mercy for a dying thief.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, remember me. I have nothing to offer You but my need. Thank You that on the cross You still had mercy for a thief, and You have mercy for me. Thank You for dying in my place. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What does the thief's story teach you about grace?
written.familyQuestion: What did Jesus say to the man on the cross next to Him?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, thank You for dying for us. Remember us in Your kingdom.

written.title: Holy Saturday: Sealing the stone
written.reflection:
The day after the crucifixion, the chief priests asked Pilate to guard the tomb. They remembered that Jesus had said He would rise after three days. So they made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch.

They did everything they could to keep Him in. It was not enough. No seal, guard or stone can hold back what God has promised. Today is the day of waiting. Whatever seems sealed shut in your life, bring it to Him and wait for the morning.
written.prayer: Lord, today I wait. Some things in my life seem sealed shut, guarded, impossible. I bring them to You. Thank You that no stone could hold Jesus in the grave. Help me to wait in hope for the morning. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What in your life seems sealed shut right now?
written.familyQuestion: How do you think the disciples felt on Saturday?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to wait in hope. Nothing is too hard for You.

written.title: Easter Sunday: He is risen
written.reflection:
At dawn, the women came to the tomb. There was an earthquake, and an angel rolled back the stone and sat on it. The guards shook with fear.

The angel said, Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified. He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. As he said. Every promise Jesus made is now proven true. Then the angel told them, go quickly, and tell. Good news is for sharing. He is risen indeed.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are risen, as You said. Thank You that death could not hold You. Thank You that every promise You made is true. Fill me with joy today, and give me courage to go and tell. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who will you tell that Jesus is risen?
written.familyQuestion: Why is Easter the happiest day for Christians?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, You are alive! Thank You. Fill our home with Easter joy.

challenges.title: Ten Days to Pentecost
challenges.promise: Wait and pray, as the first disciples did, for the Holy Spirit.

written.title: Taken up
written.reflection:
Forty days after Easter, Jesus was taken up into heaven while His disciples watched. Two men in white asked them, why stand ye gazing up into heaven?

They were told He would come again in the same way. Until then, there was work to do and a promise to wait for. These ten days follow the disciples between the Ascension and Pentecost. They did not know exactly what was coming. They only knew to wait and pray. That is a good place to start.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You have gone up into heaven, and You will come again. Keep me from standing and staring when there is work to do. Over these ten days, teach me to wait and pray for Your Spirit. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What do you hope God will do in you over these ten days?
written.familyQuestion: Where did Jesus go when He was taken up?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, thank You that You are in heaven and that You will come again.

written.title: Wait for the promise
written.reflection:
Jesus told His disciples to wait for the promise of the Father. They wanted to know about times and kingdoms. He said that was not for them to know. What they needed was power from the Holy Ghost.

Waiting is hard for most of us. We want to get on with things. But Jesus knew that working without the Spirit would be working in our own strength. Some things are worth waiting for. The Spirit is the greatest of them.
written.prayer: Father, I wait for Your promise. Forgive me for rushing ahead in my own strength. I want the power that only Your Holy Spirit can give. Teach me to wait well. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where are you rushing ahead in your own strength?
written.familyQuestion: Why is waiting hard?
written.familyPrayer: Father, help us to wait for You, and fill us with Your Spirit.

written.title: With one accord
written.reflection:
After Jesus was taken up, the disciples went back to Jerusalem to an upper room. These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus.

Men and women, old friends and family, all praying together. The Spirit came on a church that was praying with one accord. If you can, pray with others during these days: your family, a friend, a small group. Something happens when believers pray together.
written.prayer: Lord, I thank You for the people I can pray with. Bring us together in one accord. Where there is division in my family or church, heal it. Let us wait and pray together for Your Spirit. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who could you pray with during these ten days?
written.familyQuestion: When could we pray together as a family this week?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, make us one as we pray together.

written.title: It is expedient
written.reflection:
The disciples were sad that Jesus was leaving. He told them, It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you.

It is better, Jesus said, to have the Spirit with you than to have Jesus beside you in the flesh. That is a staggering thought. The Spirit is not second best. Through Him, Jesus is with every believer, everywhere, all at once. You are not missing out.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for sending the Comforter. Help me to believe that the Spirit's presence with me is not second best. Make me aware of Him today. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Do you ever wish you had lived when Jesus was on earth?
written.familyQuestion: Who did Jesus send to be with us?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, thank You for sending the Holy Spirit to be with us.

written.title: A new heart
written.reflection:
Centuries before Pentecost, God promised, A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh.

A stony heart is hard, cold and unresponsive. God does not ask us to soften it ourselves. He promises to replace it. I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes. The Spirit does in us what we cannot do: He gives us a heart that wants to obey.
written.prayer: Father, take away my stony heart and give me a heart of flesh. Put Your Spirit within me. Cause me to walk in Your ways, not by force, but by a heart that wants to. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where has your heart grown hard?
written.familyQuestion: What is the difference between a heart of stone and a heart of flesh?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, give us soft hearts that love You and love each other.

written.title: Breath on dry bones
written.reflection:
Ezekiel saw a valley full of dry bones. God told him to prophesy, and the bones came together, with sinews and flesh. but there was no breath in them.

Then God said, prophesy to the wind. the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army. A body without breath is not alive. A church, or a life, without the Spirit is the same. Pray for breath today, for yourself and for any place that feels dry.
written.prayer: Breath of God, come from the four winds and breathe on me. Where my faith feels dry, bring life. Breathe on my church, my family and my nation. Let us stand up and live. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What part of your life feels like dry bones?
written.familyQuestion: What does breath do for a body?
written.familyPrayer: Holy Spirit, breathe new life into our family.

written.title: Upon all flesh
written.reflection:
I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions.

All flesh. Sons and daughters. Old and young. Even servants and handmaids. In Israel, the Spirit came on a few chosen leaders. Joel promised a day when He would come on every kind of person. Peter would quote this on the day of Pentecost. The Spirit is for you too.
written.prayer: Father, thank You that You promised Your Spirit to all flesh, young and old, men and women. Pour out Your Spirit on me. Pour Him out on my sons and daughters, on the old and the young in my church. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Do you believe the Spirit is for you?
written.familyQuestion: What dreams do we have for God?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, pour out Your Spirit on every person in this house, young and old.

written.title: Ask Him
written.reflection:
Jesus asked, what father would give his son a stone when he asked for bread, or a snake when he asked for a fish? If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?

Some people are afraid of the Holy Spirit, unsure what they might get. Jesus says your Father gives good gifts. You can ask Him for His Spirit with confidence. He will not give you anything harmful.
written.prayer: Heavenly Father, I ask You for Your Holy Spirit. I trust that You give good gifts. Take away any fear I have. Fill me with Your Spirit, today and every day. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What makes you hesitant to ask God for more of His Spirit?
written.familyQuestion: What good gifts has God given us?
written.familyPrayer: Father, thank You for good gifts. Fill us with Your Holy Spirit.

written.title: Peace be unto you
written.reflection:
On the evening of the resurrection, the disciples were behind locked doors, afraid. Jesus came and stood among them and said, Peace be unto you. He showed them His hands and side.

Then He said, as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you, and He breathed on them: Receive ye the Holy Ghost. The Spirit is given to frightened people behind locked doors, and He sends them out. If you are afraid, you are exactly who He comes to.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, come into the locked rooms of my fear. Speak peace to me. Breathe on me, and let me receive Your Holy Spirit. Send me out as the Father sent You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What locked doors of fear do you need Jesus to come through?
written.familyQuestion: What did Jesus say when He came to His friends?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, give our family Your peace, and send us out to share it.

written.title: Pentecost: All filled
written.reflection:
when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. Then came the sound of a rushing mighty wind and tongues like fire, And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost.

All. Not just the apostles. Everyone who had been waiting and praying. Pentecost is sometimes called the birthday of the church. The Spirit who came that day is still given today to everyone who believes. Thank God for Him, and ask to be filled again.
written.prayer: Holy Spirit, thank You for coming on the day of Pentecost, and thank You that You are still given today. Fill me again. Let Your fire burn in me. Give me words to speak of the wonderful works of God. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: How will you live differently, knowing the Spirit is with you?
written.familyQuestion: Why is Pentecost called the birthday of the church?
written.familyPrayer: Holy Spirit, fill us all. Thank You for the church, God's family.

challenges.title: Advent: Waiting for Christ
challenges.promise: One reading a day from the first promise in Genesis to the shepherds' field on Christmas Eve.

written.title: The first promise
written.reflection:
Advent means coming. For twenty-four days we wait, as God's people waited for centuries, for the coming of Christ.

The waiting begins here, in the garden, just after the first sin. God speaks to the serpent: I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. Even in judgment, God made a promise. One would come from the woman to crush evil, though He would be wounded doing it.
written.prayer: Father, thank You that from the very beginning You had a plan to save us. Even when we first turned from You, You made a promise. As I begin Advent, teach me to wait for Christ with hope. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What are you waiting for this Christmas, apart from presents?
written.familyQuestion: What does the word Advent mean?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, as we wait for Christmas, help us to wait for Jesus.

written.title: All families of the earth
written.reflection:
God called Abram to leave his country and go to a land He would show him. He promised to make him a great nation and to bless him. Then came the promise that reaches all the way to us: in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

All families. Every nation, every tribe, every language. Through Abraham's family, Jesus would come, and through Him, the blessing would reach the whole world. Your family is one of the families God had in mind.
written.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your promise to Abraham was for all families of the earth, including mine. Thank You that the blessing came through Jesus. Help my family to be a blessing to others this season. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: How has your family been blessed through Jesus?
written.familyQuestion: Which family could we bless this Christmas?
written.familyPrayer: Father, thank You for blessing our family. Help us to bless others.

written.title: A throne for ever
written.reflection:
David wanted to build God a house. Instead, God promised to build David a house, a family line that would last. thy throne shall be established for ever.

David's kingdom rose and fell. His descendants were often unfaithful. For a long time it looked as if the promise had failed. But God was keeping it. A thousand years later, an angel told Mary that her son would be given the throne of his father David. God's promises can look broken for centuries and still come true.
written.prayer: Lord, You keep Your promises, even when they seem forgotten. Thank You that Jesus is the King on David's throne for ever. Where I think Your promises to me have failed, help me to wait. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Is there a promise of God you have stopped believing?
written.familyQuestion: Who was King David's famous descendant?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You that Jesus is King for ever.

written.title: Immanuel
written.reflection:
King Ahaz was afraid and would not trust God. So God gave him a sign anyway: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

Immanuel means God with us. Not God far above us, or God disappointed with us, but God with us. That is the heart of Christmas. Whatever you are facing this December, you do not face it alone. The name of the child is the promise.
written.prayer: Lord, thank You that You are Immanuel, God with us. Thank You that You came close. Whatever I face this month, help me to remember that You are with me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where do you most need to know that God is with you?
