written.familyQuestion: What does Immanuel mean?
written.familyPrayer: Immanuel, thank You for being with our family.

written.title: A great light
written.reflection:
The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.

December can be a dark month, whether in short northern days or in hard seasons of life. Some people find Christmas painful: the empty chair, the money worries, the loneliness. Isaiah does not say the darkness was not real. He says light came into it. Jesus did not wait for the world to be bright before He came.
written.prayer: Lord, I bring You the dark places in my life and in my world. Thank You that Jesus came as a great light into the darkness. Shine on me, and on everyone who finds this season hard. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who do you know who finds this season hard?
written.familyQuestion: Why do we put up lights at Christmas?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, shine Your light on everyone who feels sad this Christmas.

written.title: Unto us a child is born
written.reflection:
For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given. A child born, a son given. He was born as one of us, and He was given from heaven.

Then come His names: Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace. Each name is a gift. Which do you need most today? A counsellor for your decisions? A mighty God for your battles? A Prince of Peace for your heart? He is all of them.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are Wonderful, Counsellor, the mighty God, the everlasting Father, the Prince of Peace. I need You as my counsellor and my peace today. Let the government of my life be on Your shoulder. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Which of Jesus' names do you need most today?
written.familyQuestion: Which name for Jesus do we like best?
written.familyPrayer: Prince of Peace, bring Your peace to our home.

written.title: A rod out of the stem of Jesse
written.reflection:
there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots. Jesse was David's father. By Isaiah's time, the family tree looked like a stump, cut down.

But God promised a green shoot from the stump. the spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him. He would judge the poor with righteousness. God often brings new life from what looks dead. If something in your life feels like a stump, do not give up on it.
written.prayer: Lord, thank You that new life came from the stump of Jesse. Where my life feels cut down, bring a green shoot. Thank You that Jesus judges the poor with righteousness and is faithful. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What in your life feels like a stump?
written.familyQuestion: What grows out of a cut-down tree?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, bring new life to every place in our family that feels cut down.

written.title: Little Bethlehem
written.reflection:
But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel.

God chose a small town for the birth of His Son. Not Rome, not Jerusalem, but Bethlehem, little among the thousands. And the ruler who came from there has goings forth that have been from of old, from everlasting. The eternal God entered the world through a small place. He is not put off by small things. He chooses them.
written.prayer: Lord, thank You that You chose little Bethlehem. Thank You that You are not put off by small or overlooked places. Come into the small places of my life and make them Yours. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Do you ever feel too small for God to use?
written.familyQuestion: Where was Jesus born?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You that You love small and ordinary things.

written.title: The LORD our righteousness
written.reflection:
Israel's kings had failed again and again. Jeremiah promised a different kind of king: a righteous Branch, who would execute judgment and justice in the earth.

Then his name: THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS. Not only a righteous king who would demand righteousness from us, but one who would be our righteousness. We cannot make ourselves right with God. Christ came to give us His own righteousness as a gift. That is the best present anyone will be given this Christmas.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the Lord our righteousness. I cannot make myself right with God, but You have given me Your righteousness as a gift. Thank You. Reign in my life with justice and goodness. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What does it mean that Jesus is your righteousness?
written.familyQuestion: What is the best gift God has given us?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, thank You for making us right with God.

written.title: Comfort ye
written.reflection:
Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God. After chapters of warning, God speaks tenderly. The hard season is over. Sins are pardoned.

Then a voice cries, Prepare ye the way of the LORD. Valleys lifted, mountains made low, rough places made plain. Advent is a time to prepare: not only the house and the food, but the heart. What needs to be lifted, levelled or made straight in you before Christmas?
written.prayer: Lord, comfort me today. Thank You that my sins are pardoned. Prepare the way in my heart for You. Lift what is low, bring down what is proud, and make the rough places plain. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What needs to be prepared in your heart before Christmas?
written.familyQuestion: How are we preparing for Christmas in our home?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, as we prepare our house for Christmas, prepare our hearts for You.

written.title: Like a shepherd
written.reflection:
Isaiah calls out, Behold your God! The Lord God comes with strong hand. And then, a surprise: He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young.

Strong and gentle. Mighty and tender. That is the God who came at Christmas. He carries the lambs. He is gentle with mothers. If you feel weak or worn out this season, let Him carry you.
written.prayer: Lord, thank You that You are strong and gentle. Gather me in Your arms like a lamb. Gently lead those who are tired, those who are carrying young children, and those who are worn out this season. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where do you need God to carry you?
written.familyQuestion: How does a shepherd look after little lambs?
written.familyPrayer: Good Shepherd, carry each one of us, and be gentle with the tired.

written.title: Your God will come
written.reflection:
Isaiah paints a desert bursting into bloom. Then he says, Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees. Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come.

And when He comes, the eyes of the blind shall be opened. Jesus did exactly these things. Is your heart fearful today? This is a word for you, and a word to pass on to someone else whose knees are shaking. God has come, and He will come again.
written.prayer: Lord, strengthen my weak hands and my feeble knees. To my fearful heart, say, be strong, fear not. Thank You that You came, and that You will come again. Help me to encourage someone else today. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who could you encourage with these words today?
written.familyQuestion: What happened to blind and lame people when Jesus came?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, make us strong and brave, and help us to encourage others.

written.title: The messenger
written.reflection:
Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me. This was fulfilled in John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Jesus.

But Malachi also asks, who may abide the day of his coming? The Lord comes like a refiner's fire. A refiner heats silver to burn away what is impure. Christ's coming is good news, but it is not comfortable news. He comes to make us pure, not to leave us as we are.
written.prayer: Lord, I welcome You, even as a refiner's fire. Burn away what is impure in me. Thank You that You refine me because You love me and want to make me like silver. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What might God want to refine in you?
written.familyQuestion: Who prepared the way for Jesus?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, make us pure and good, like silver made shiny.

written.title: Arise, shine
written.reflection:
Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee. Darkness covers the earth, but the Lord shines on His people.

Then, the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising. The wise men from the east were among the first to come. The light of Christ is not for us to keep. It shines on us so that others can find their way to Him. How could your life shine this Christmas?
written.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your light has come and Your glory has risen on me. Help me to arise and shine, so that others may come to Your light through me this Christmas. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: How could your life shine for others this Christmas?
written.familyQuestion: Who followed a star to find Jesus?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help our family to shine with Your light.

written.title: Beautiful feet
written.reflection:
How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace. In those days news came by runners. A messenger with good news was the most welcome sight.

The news is this: Thy God reigneth! At Christmas, many people are more open than usual to hearing about Jesus. Could you be a messenger with beautiful feet? Invite someone to a carol service. Tell them why Christmas matters to you.
written.prayer: Lord, give me beautiful feet. Let me carry good news this Christmas. Show me who to invite, who to tell, and give me courage and kindness when I do. Thy God reigneth! In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who could you invite to church or tell about Jesus this Christmas?
written.familyQuestion: What is the good news of Christmas?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to share the good news of Jesus with our friends.

written.title: Thy prayer is heard
written.reflection:
Zacharias and Elisabeth were righteous and old, and they had no child. They had surely prayed for one for years. While Zacharias was serving in the temple, an angel appeared: Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard.

The prayer may have been decades old. He may have stopped praying it. But God had not forgotten. The silence of four hundred years between the prophets and this moment was ending. If you have an old prayer, keep praying it.
written.prayer: Father, thank You that You hear prayers that are years old. I bring You my oldest prayer again. Thank You that You do not forget. Give me faith to keep praying and patience to wait for Your time. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What old prayer do you still carry?
written.familyQuestion: What did the angel tell Zacharias?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You that You hear every prayer, even old ones.

written.title: Blessed is she that believed
written.reflection:
Mary hurried to see her cousin Elisabeth. When Elisabeth heard her greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and she was filled with the Holy Ghost. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.

Then she said, blessed is she that believed. Mary was blessed not only for being chosen but for believing. She trusted that God would do what He said. Two women, one old and one young, encouraged each other in faith. Who encourages you?
written.prayer: Lord, thank You for people who encourage my faith. Make me someone who encourages others. Help me to believe, as Mary did, that You will do what You have said. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who encourages your faith, and who could you encourage?
written.familyQuestion: Why did baby John jump for joy?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to encourage each other to trust You.

written.title: Joseph's dream
written.reflection:
Joseph found out that Mary was expecting a child that was not his. He was a just man, and he decided to end the engagement quietly, to protect her from shame.

Then an angel spoke to him in a dream: fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife. And: thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. Joseph obeyed. He faced gossip and misunderstanding. Quiet obedience, like Joseph's, is often what God uses most.
written.prayer: Lord, thank You for Joseph's quiet faithfulness. Give me the same courage to obey You when others do not understand. Thank You that Jesus came to save His people from their sins, including me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where is God asking you to obey quietly, even if others misunderstand?
written.familyQuestion: What does the name Jesus mean?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to obey You, even when it is hard.

written.title: God with us
written.reflection:
Matthew looks back at Isaiah's words and sees them fulfilled: they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us.

Joseph woke up and did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him. He took Mary as his wife, and when the child was born, he called his name JESUS. Seven hundred years after Isaiah, the promise was kept. God with us was no longer a hope. He was a baby in a young family, about to be born.
written.prayer: Emmanuel, God with us, thank You that the promise was kept. Thank You that You did not stay far away but came to be with us. Be with me today, and let me be aware of You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: How does it change things to know God is with you?
written.familyQuestion: Who named baby Jesus?
written.familyPrayer: Emmanuel, thank You that You are with us every day.

written.title: The dayspring from on high
written.reflection:
When John was born, Zacharias' tongue was loosed, and he praised God. He sang that his son would prepare the way for the Lord.

Then he described what was coming: the dayspring from on high hath visited us, To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace. Dayspring means the dawn. After a long night, the sun was about to rise. Christmas is the dawn.
written.prayer: Lord, thank You for the dayspring from on high. Thank You for Your tender mercy. Give light to all who sit in darkness this Christmas, and guide my feet into the way of peace. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where do you need the dawn to break?
written.familyQuestion: What happens when the sun rises in the morning?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, guide our feet into the way of peace.

written.title: The fulness of the time
written.reflection:
when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman. God's timing was exact. Not too early, not too late.

And He came To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. Christmas is not only about a baby. It is about God making us His children. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son. The Son of God became a son of man so that we could become sons and daughters of God.
written.prayer: Father, thank You that You sent Your Son at just the right time. Thank You that through Him I am no longer a servant but Your child and heir. Help me to trust Your timing in my own life too. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Where do you need to trust God's timing?
written.familyQuestion: What does it mean to be adopted into God's family?
written.familyPrayer: Father, thank You that we are Your children.

written.title: In the beginning was the Word
written.reflection:
John begins the story of Jesus not in Bethlehem but before time. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

The baby in the manger made the stars. All things were made by him. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not. The darkness could not understand it, and could not put it out. With Christmas nearly here, remember who it is that comes. The Creator is coming to His creation.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the eternal Word. You made all things, and You came into the world You made. Thank You that Your light shines in the darkness, and the darkness cannot overcome it. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What does it mean to you that the baby in the manger is the Creator?
written.familyQuestion: Who made the stars?
written.familyPrayer: Lord Jesus, You made everything, and You came to be with us. Thank You.

written.title: The Word was made flesh
written.reflection:
He came unto his own, and his own received him not. Many did not want Him. But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God.

Then the great sentence of Christmas: the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us. God took on skin. He was hungry, tired and cold. He knows what it is to be human. Tomorrow we remember His birth. Today, make sure there is room for Him. Receive Him again.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You came to Your own, and many did not receive You. I receive You today. Thank You that the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us. Make Your home in me this Christmas. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Is there room for Jesus in your Christmas?
written.familyQuestion: How can we make room for Jesus this Christmas?
written.familyPrayer: Jesus, we receive You. Make Your home with us.

written.title: Christmas Eve: Good tidings of great joy
written.reflection:
Shepherds were working the night shift on the hills outside Bethlehem when the sky filled with light. Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.

For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord. Unto you. The waiting is over. The promise from the garden, to Abraham, to David, through all the prophets, is kept tonight. Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.
written.prayer: Glory to God in the highest! Thank You, Father, for the Saviour born in Bethlehem. Thank You that the good tidings are for all people, and for me. Fill my home with joy and peace tonight. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What does it mean to you that a Saviour was born unto you?
written.familyQuestion: What did the angels sing to the shepherds?
written.familyPrayer: Glory to God! Thank You for Jesus. Fill our home with joy tonight.

challenges.title: Seven Days of Thanksgiving
challenges.promise: A week to count your blessings out loud and thank the One they came from.

written.title: Come before Him with thanksgiving
written.reflection:
Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms. The psalm does not begin with requests. It begins with thanks and singing, because the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods.

For seven days, try beginning every prayer with thanks before you ask for anything. It may feel strange at first. But thanksgiving changes the way we see our needs. It reminds us who we are talking to.
written.prayer: Lord, I come before Your presence with thanksgiving. You are a great God and a great King. Before I ask You for anything today, I thank You for who You are and for all You have done. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What would change if you began every prayer this week with thanks?
written.familyQuestion: What is one thing each of us is thankful for today?
written.familyPrayer: Thank You, Lord, for this family and for everything You give us.

written.title: When thou hast eaten
written.reflection:
When thou hast eaten and art full, then thou shalt bless the LORD thy God for the good land which he hath given thee. The very next verse warns, Beware that thou forget not the LORD thy God.

Full stomachs can lead to forgetful hearts. When things are going well, it is easy to forget where they came from. Many families give thanks before meals. Today, try giving thanks after the meal too, when you are full. It is a simple way to remember.
written.prayer: Father, thank You for food on my table. When I am full, let me not forget You. Thank You for every good thing You have given me. Keep my heart grateful in plenty as well as in need. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: When are you most likely to forget God?
written.familyQuestion: Can we thank God after our meal today, as well as before?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You for our food. Help us never to forget that it comes from You.

written.title: In every thing
written.reflection:
In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you. In every thing, not for every thing. We do not thank God for sickness or loss. But even in them, there is something to thank Him for: His presence, His promises, the people who stand with us.

People often wonder what God's will is for their lives. Here is part of the answer, plainly written: rejoice, pray and give thanks. You can begin doing His will today.
written.prayer: Lord, help me to give thanks in every thing, even in the hard things I am facing. Show me where You are present in them. Thank You that rejoicing, praying and giving thanks are Your will for me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What hard thing could you still find something to thank God for in?
written.familyQuestion: What is something good that happened on a hard day?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to be thankful on hard days as well as good ones.

written.title: What shall I render?
written.reflection:
What shall I render unto the LORD for all his benefits toward me? The psalmist had been rescued from death, and he wanted to give something back.

His answer is surprising. I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the LORD. The first thing he gives is to receive more. We thank God best by trusting Him more, calling on Him again and keeping our promises to Him in front of others. Gratitude becomes worship.
written.prayer: Lord, what can I give You for all Your goodness to me? I take the cup of salvation again and call on Your name. I will keep my promises to You. Let my gratitude become worship. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What promise to God do you want to keep?
written.familyQuestion: What could we give back to God this week?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You for all Your goodness. We give You our love and our lives.

written.title: His unspeakable gift
written.reflection:
Paul was collecting a gift from the churches for poor believers in Jerusalem. He says their generosity would overflow by many thanksgivings unto God. Giving leads to thanks. Then he ends with a burst of praise: Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.

The unspeakable gift is Jesus, a gift too great for words. Every other thing we thank God for flows from this one. Today, thank Him for Jesus. And think of someone your generosity could cause to give thanks.
written.prayer: Thanks be to You, God, for Your unspeakable gift, Jesus Christ. Every good thing I have comes through Him. Make me generous, so that others will give thanks to You because of what I give. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Whose thanksgiving could your generosity cause this week?
written.familyQuestion: What is the best gift God has ever given?
written.familyPrayer: Thank You, God, for Jesus. Help us to give to others too.

written.title: As he did aforetime
written.reflection:
Daniel knew a law had been signed against praying to anyone but the king. He went home, opened his windows toward Jerusalem, knelt three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.

He gave thanks, knowing the lions' den was waiting. And he did it as he did aforetime. It was not new. It was his habit. Gratitude that holds up under pressure is built on ordinary days. What habit of thanks could you build?
written.prayer: Lord, give me a habit of thanksgiving that holds up under pressure. Like Daniel, let me give thanks to You whatever is happening around me. Help me to build it on ordinary days. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What daily habit of thanks could you begin?
written.familyQuestion: When could we thank God together every day?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help us to thank You every day, in good times and in hard times.

written.title: At all times
written.reflection:
I will bless the LORD at all times: his praise shall continually be in my mouth. David wrote this after escaping from danger by pretending to be mad. Not his finest hour. Yet he praised God.

Then he invites others: O magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt his name together. Gratitude grows when it is shared. As this week ends, invite someone to give thanks with you. Tell each other what God has done. And the humble shall hear thereof, and be glad.
written.prayer: Lord, I will bless You at all times. Let Your praise be continually in my mouth, not only this week but every week. Help me to invite others to magnify You with me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who will you invite to give thanks with you?
written.familyQuestion: What has God done for our family this year?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, we bless You at all times. Thank You for this year together.

challenges.title: A Week for Students
challenges.promise: Seven days for the start of a school or university year: friends, study, faith and nerves.

written.title: Remember thy Creator
written.reflection:
Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth. A new school year is full of new things: classes, teachers, timetables, friends. In all of it, it is easy to forget God until something goes wrong.

The Preacher says, remember Him now, while you are young. Not later when life slows down. Faith built now will hold you when hard days come. Begin this year by giving it to the God who made you and knows you.
written.prayer: Lord, I remember You at the start of this year. You made me and You know me. I give You my studies, my friendships and my future. Be part of every day of this year, not just the hard ones. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What are you most excited or nervous about this year?
written.familyQuestion: What is each of us looking forward to this school year?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, bless every student in this house this year. Be with them every day.

written.title: Hid in mine heart
written.reflection:
Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. The psalmist asks how a young person can stay on the right path. The answer is God's word.

Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee. You will face pressure this year to go along with things you know are wrong. A verse you have memorised can come back to you in that moment. Choose one to learn this week.
written.prayer: Lord, I want to hide Your word in my heart. Help me to learn it and remember it. When I face pressure to do wrong, bring Your word back to me. Keep me from wandering from You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Which verse will you learn this week?
written.familyQuestion: Can we learn a verse together this week?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help our children to love Your word and remember it.

written.title: Purposed in his heart
written.reflection:
Daniel was a teenager taken to a foreign land and put in the king's school. The food and the ways were not God's ways. But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself.

He decided ahead of time. Then he asked respectfully, and God gave him favour. It is easier to say no in the moment if you have already decided. What will you decide now about how you will live this year, before the pressure comes?
written.prayer: Lord, like Daniel, I purpose in my heart to honour You this year. Help me to decide now what I will and will not do. Give me courage to stand, and give me favour with my teachers and classmates. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What will you decide now, before the pressure comes?
written.familyQuestion: What are some things we have decided as a family?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, give our children courage to stand for what is right, and favour with others.

written.title: The beginning of knowledge
written.reflection:
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge. You will learn a great deal this year: facts, skills, ideas. Proverbs says that real knowledge starts with honouring God.

Then it speaks to the young: hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother. Some of the wisest lessons will not come from textbooks. They will come from parents, grandparents and others who love you and have walked further. Listen to them.
written.prayer: Lord, let my learning begin with honouring You. Give me a humble heart to learn from my teachers and from those who love me. Make me wise, not just clever. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Whose advice do you find hardest to listen to?
written.familyQuestion: What is something wise a grandparent or parent has taught us?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, make our children wise, and help us to teach them well.

written.title: Good friends
written.reflection:
Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. In plain English: bad company ruins good character. The friends you choose this year will shape you more than almost anything else.

This does not mean avoiding everyone who is not a Christian. Jesus was a friend of sinners. But your closest friends, the ones you follow, matter. Pray for good friends. And pray that you would be a good friend to someone who needs one.
written.prayer: Lord, give me good friends this year, friends who help me to be who You made me to be. Help me to be a good friend too. Show me someone who is lonely, and give me courage to be kind. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who are the friends who shape you most?
written.familyQuestion: Who at school might need a friend?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, give our children good friends, and make them kind to the lonely.

written.title: Increased in wisdom
written.reflection:
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man. This is almost all we know of Jesus between the ages of twelve and thirty. He grew.

He grew in wisdom, His mind. In stature, His body. In favour with God, His faith. And with man, His relationships. Growth in all four is what a good year looks like. Not only top marks, but a whole person growing. Which area do you want to grow in this year?
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, You grew in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man. Help me to grow like that this year: in my mind, my body, my faith and my friendships. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Which of the four areas do you most want to grow in this year?
written.familyQuestion: How have we each grown this past year?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, help each of us to grow in wisdom, in body, in faith and in kindness.

written.title: Good success
written.reflection:
God told Joshua to keep His word in his mouth and meditate therein day and night, and then thou shalt have good success.

Good success is more than passing exams. It is a life that pleases God. And God follows the promise with another: Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest. Into every classroom, every exam hall, every new friendship, He goes with you.
written.prayer: Lord, I want good success this year, the kind that pleases You. Help me to keep Your word close. Make me strong and courageous. Thank You that You are with me wherever I go, in every classroom and every exam. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What would good success look like for you this year?
written.familyQuestion: How can we pray for each other through this year?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, be with our students wherever they go. Give them good success.

challenges.title: Honour Your Parents
challenges.promise: Five days around Mother's Day and Father's Day, for thanks, for healing, and for the parents growing old.

written.title: The first commandment with promise
written.reflection:
Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;). Paul points back to the Ten Commandments and notices that this one comes with a promise: That it may be well with thee.

Honour is not the same as agreeing with everything your parents say or do. It means treating them with respect, speaking well of them, and caring for them. It applies whether you are seven or seventy. Today, think of one way you could honour your parents this week.
written.prayer: Father God, thank You for my parents. Help me to honour them in my words and actions, whatever their age and mine. Show me one way I can honour them this week. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What is one way you could honour your parents this week?
written.familyQuestion: What does it mean to honour someone?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You for parents. Help us to honour and love each other.

written.title: When she is old
written.reflection:
Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old. Parents grow old. They may become slow, forgetful or difficult. It is easy to grow impatient with them.

Proverbs says, do not despise them. In many cultures, caring for ageing parents is simply what children do. In others, it is easy to leave it to someone else. Either way, God sees how we treat those who once cared for us. Call your parents, or visit them, this week.
written.prayer: Lord, I pray for my parents as they grow older. Give me patience and kindness toward them. Help me not to despise them when they are slow or difficult. Show me how to care for them well. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: How could you show care for an older parent or relative this week?
written.familyQuestion: Which grandparent or older relative could we call or visit?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, bless our grandparents and older relatives. Help us to care for them.

written.title: Her children arise up
written.reflection:
Proverbs ends with a portrait of a woman of strength and wisdom: Strength and honour are her clothing. She works hard, speaks with kindness and cares for her household. Her children arise up, and call her blessed.

Many mothers, grandmothers and women who have mothered us carry heavy loads with little thanks. Today, rise up and call them blessed. Tell them what they mean to you. Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.
written.prayer: Lord, thank You for the mothers and the women who have cared for me. Bless them with strength and honour. Help me to rise up and call them blessed, and to thank them in words they can hear. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Who has mothered you, and how could you thank her?
written.familyQuestion: What do we love about the mothers in our family?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, bless the mothers and grandmothers in our family. Thank You for them.

written.title: When my father and my mother forsake me
written.reflection:
Not everyone has parents who were kind. Some were absent, harsh or worse. If that is your story, days like Mother's Day and Father's Day can hurt.

David wrote, When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up. God is the Father who does not leave. He sees what was done to you. Honouring your parents does not mean pretending the hurt did not happen. You can bring your pain to God and let Him take you up.
written.prayer: Lord, You know my story with my parents, the good and the painful. Where I was let down, take me up. Heal what was broken. Help me to honour my parents where I can, and to forgive where I must. You are my Father. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: What do you need to bring to God about your parents?
written.familyQuestion: Who has been like a parent to us when we needed one?
written.familyPrayer: Lord, thank You that You are our Father who never leaves.

written.title: Behold thy mother
written.reflection:
On the cross, in terrible pain, Jesus saw His mother standing nearby. He said to her, Woman, behold thy son!, and to John, Behold thy mother! From that hour John took her into his home.

While He was saving the world, Jesus made sure His mother would be cared for. Honouring parents is not too small a thing for the Son of God. Let His example shape how you care for your own parents, and for older people in your church who have no one.
written.prayer: Lord Jesus, even on the cross You cared for Your mother. Help me to care for my parents as You cared for Yours. Show me older people in my church and community who have no one, and help me to love them. In Jesus' name, Amen.
written.question: Is there an older person in your church who has no family nearby?
written.familyQuestion: How did Jesus look after His mother?
written.familyPrayer: Lord Jesus, help us to care for our parents and for older people who are alone.
